translationRepairs: This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's grandson Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
This section covers Miao Jinqing, Pei Mian, and Pei Zunqing, together with Pei Xiang, Xiang's son Yin, and Yin's son Shu. Miao Jinqing was from Huguan in Shangdang.
s0001 寅子樞 is Yin's son Shu; grandson invents a generation beyond 子.
His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
His grandfather Kui, a man of exalted principle who never held office, was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
s0003 追贈禮部尚書 is a posthumous office grant; 追贈 is not territorial enfeoffment (封), and the replacement states that accurately.
For more than twenty years the realm has endured deep trial; through that anguish Heaven has prepared a sage ruler—and today is the day.
For more than twenty years he has upheld primal rectitude over the myriad states; through grave anguish Heaven opens the way to sage rule—and today is that day.
s0106 元貞萬國，二十余年 names long upright stewardship of the myriad states; the original drops that sense and folds the twenty years into 殷憂 alone. The replacement restores both halves before 殷憂啟聖.
The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand mentor, and granted five hundred bolts of funeral silk and five hundred shi of grain.
The emperor mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant, and granted five hundred bolts of funeral silk and five hundred shi of grain.
s0134 贈太尉 is the posthumous honor Grand Commandant; Grand Mentor would be 太傅, so the title must be corrected.
The sovereign mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Mentor, and granted funeral silks of five hundred bolts and five hundred shi of grain.
The sovereign mourned him, halted court for three days, posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant, and granted funeral silks of five hundred bolts and five hundred shi of grain.
Same unit: 贈太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Mentor, and 贈 marks posthumous honor rather than enfeoffment.
When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed drafting secretary, right assistant in the Secretariat, and vice minister of personnel.
When Suzong took the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed supervising secretary, right assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and vice minister of personnel.
s0144 給事中 is Supervising Secretary, not Drafting Secretary (中書舍人); 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs (尚書省), not the Secretariat.
When Suzong ascended the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed Drafting Secretary, Right Assistant in the Secretariat, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
When Suzong ascended the throne, Zunqing was summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary, Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs, and Vice Minister of Personnel.
Same unit: 給事中 and 尚書右丞 are Supervising Secretary and Right Assistant of the Department of State Affairs; the literal replacement matches those offices.

Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huai'guang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.

Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
李懷光 is Li Huaiguang; the apostrophe in Huai'guang is nonstandard pinyin (not needed before g) and should be removed.

He was posthumously enfeoffed as junior mentor to the heir apparent.
He was posthumously granted the title of junior mentor to the heir apparent.
s0178 贈太子少保 is a posthumous title grant; 贈 is not territorial enfeoffment.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
He was posthumously granted the title of Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
Same unit: 贈 marks a posthumous title grant, not enfeoffment; the literal replacement matches that sense.
In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate of the heir apparent, soon sent out as prefect of She.
In Dashun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made right subordinate of the heir apparent, soon sent out as prefect of She.
s0188 大順 is the Tang reign Dashun; Dazhun misreads 順.
In Dazhun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
In Dashun, Wei was demoted for military failure without achievement; Shu was implicated and made Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, soon sent out as Prefect of She.
Same unit: 大順 is Dashun, not Dazhun; the literal replacement restores the reign name.
Zunqing and his son and grandson—few could match them.
Zunqing and his son—few could match them.
s0223 遵慶父子 is Zunqing and his son(s); "son and grandson" invents a generation absent from 父子.
Zunqing and his line—few could equal them.
Zunqing and his son—few could equal them.
父子 names the father-son pair, not a vague multi-generation "line"; "Zunqing and his son" matches the Chinese.
